## Cyclic Binder

Design cyclic peptide binders against a selected target chain.

### Public interface guidance

Design cyclic peptide binder candidates against a selected protein chain in a target PDB structure. Specify the target chain and peptide length to guide structure-based peptide design.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: cyclic_binder. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `pdb_path` | string | Required | file | Target protein structure as a PDB file. The structure must contain the chain selected in target_chain. |
| `target_chain` | string | Required | value | Single-character identifier of the protein target chain in the uploaded PDB. |
| `binder_len` | string | Required | value | Length of the cyclic peptide to design, in amino acids. Enter an integer from 3 through 100. For API requests, send a JSON integer rather than quoted numeric text. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: Generated peptide–target structures and design-run outputs. Predicted cyclization and interface geometry require further evaluation before synthesis or binding conclusions.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `cyclic_binder`.

## Evobind

Never invent an alignment or target residues. Download and verify the actual backend outputs before describing the generated peptides. No durable Mongo collection is inferred from this job name.

### Public interface guidance

Optimize peptide binder candidates and predicted complex structures against a target protein using EvoBind. Supply the target sequence and a matching A3M alignment. The num_peptides parameter controls optimization iterations; target_residues can focus the interface, and cyclic_offset selects linear or cyclic peptide modeling.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `job_name` | string | Required | envelope | Tool identifier: Evobind. It selects the tool, not the experiment label. The connector generates experiment_name when omitted; preserve an exact label only when supplied by the user. |
| `sequence` | string | Required | value | Target protein sequence in uppercase one-letter amino-acid codes. The 20 standard residues and X are accepted. It must match the first query sequence in the A3M alignment after removing gaps. |
| `a3m_file_path` | string | Required | file | A3M multiple-sequence alignment for the target protein. The first sequence must match sequence; preserve valid A3M alignment formatting. |
| `num_peptides` | integer | Required | value | Number of optimization iterations, supplied as an integer of at least 2. Each iteration advances the peptide-design run. This value does not specify or guarantee the number of independent peptide sequences returned. |
| `seq_length` | integer | Required | value | Requested peptide length in amino acids. Supply a positive integer for a fixed length, or 0 to use 40 residues. |
| `target_residues` | string | Required | value | Comma-separated, one-based target sequence positions used to focus the interface, for example 23,24. Include an empty string when no interface positions are specified. |
| `cyclic_offset` | string | Required | value | Select True for cyclic-peptide modeling or False for linear-peptide modeling. Lowercase true and false are also accepted. This setting controls modeled geometry. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product result guidance: A ZIP containing generated PDB structures and metrics.csv. The optimization may produce repeated or related candidates; its iteration count is not a count of independent binders.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Evobind`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | string | yes | value | Target protein amino-acid sequence. |
| `a3m_file_path` | string | yes | file | Upload the corresponding A3M alignment. |
| `num_peptides` | integer | no / mode-dependent | value | Number of peptides to generate. |
| `seq_length` | integer | no / mode-dependent | value | Generated peptide length. |
| `target_residues` | string | no / mode-dependent | value | Comma-separated target residue positions. |
| `cyclic_offset` | string | no / mode-dependent | value | Exactly `"True"` or `"False"`, not a JSON boolean. |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.

## Sequence based peptide generation

Generate candidate peptide binders conditioned on a target protein sequence using the target-based PepPrCLIP backend.

### Public interface guidance

Generate and rank peptide candidates for a supplied target protein using PepPrCLIP. Language-model-based generation produces candidates, and contrastive target-conditioned scoring ranks them against the target sequence. Supply both the candidate count and one peptide length explicitly.

This table describes the product interface. The connector's exact request schema, file checks, input limits and execution notices below remain authoritative. Product labels are not automatic API aliases or permission to use unsupported values; do not infer unverified field mappings.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | string | Required | value | Target protein amino-acid sequence used to condition peptide generation. This is the protein to bind, not a starting peptide. Uppercase standard amino acids and X, B, U, Z and O are accepted. |
| `num_peptides` | string | Required | value | Required number of peptide candidates to generate, supplied as a positive whole-number string such as "15". No default count is supplied; enter the requested value explicitly. |
| `seq_length` | string | Required | value | Required peptide length in amino acids, supplied as one whole-number string from "11" through "50". Enter a single length; no default length is supplied. |

An experiment label is generated by the connector when omitted. Keep an exact label only when the user supplied one; use the submission envelope below.

Product-interface limits (not overrides of connector validation): Choose one peptide length from 11 through 50 amino acids and a positive candidate count. Supply both values as whole-number strings.

Product result guidance: A CSV of peptide sequences, model scores and calculated properties such as molecular weight and pI. Model scores support ranking; they do not establish measured affinity or activity.

A submission acknowledgement confirms receipt; wait for completion and inspect actual artifacts before interpreting or reporting results.

Exact job name: `Sequence_based_peptide_generation`.

### Inputs

Fields below belong in `experiment_data`. The connector generates `experiment_name` unless the user supplies one.

| Field | Type | Required | Input kind | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `sequence` | string | yes | value | Antigen/target sequence. |
| `num_peptides` | string | yes | value | Requested candidate count, for example `"15"`. Preserve the plural field name. |
| `seq_length` | string | yes | value | Desired peptide length. Documented supported range is 11–50 residues. |

Input kinds: `value` is inline data; `file` requires a platform file reference;
`file_or_value` supports either documented mode; `artifact` is an authorized upstream result reference.
Only local files require a new upload. Never infer input mode from a field name.
